lessonContentPlans.lessonSummary: Introduce the major systems, professional expectations, safety boundaries, technical-information habits, and evidence-based reasoning process learners will use throughout the automotive technology curriculum.
prerequisites: No formal course prerequisite
Orientation to the AutoLearnPro learning environment

learningObjectives.statement: Identify major vehicle systems and explain their basic functional relationships without treating a system overview as a vehicle-specific service procedure.
Distinguish a customer concern, observation, measurement, technical reference, hypothesis, and diagnostic conclusion.
Use safety, professional practice, and applicable technical information to select and document an appropriate next step for a basic vehicle concern.

contentBlocks.title: Lesson targets
contentBlocks.description: Preview the systems, evidence, safety, and professional-practice outcomes for the lesson.

contentBlocks.title: What learners already know
contentBlocks.description: Activate everyday vehicle knowledge while separating informal familiarity from verified technical information.

contentBlocks.title: Vehicle systems as an interconnected whole
contentBlocks.description: Introduce major vehicle systems and the idea that a symptom in one area may depend on conditions in another.

contentBlocks.title: Vehicle-system relationship model
contentBlocks.description: Use a simplified conceptual model to connect power, control, chassis, thermal, electrical, and information functions without implying a universal vehicle architecture.

contentBlocks.title: From concern to next step
contentBlocks.description: Demonstrate how a basic vehicle concern moves from reported symptom to observation, information gathering, hypothesis, and a justified next check.

contentBlocks.title: Evidence sorting
contentBlocks.description: Classify sample statements as concern, observation, measurement, reference, hypothesis, or conclusion.

contentBlocks.title: Basic vehicle concern
contentBlocks.description: Choose a safe and information-supported next step for a simple vehicle concern without being given a repair answer.

contentBlocks.title: Foundations reasoning check
contentBlocks.description: Use low-stakes formative prompts to check system recognition, evidence classification, and next-step reasoning.

contentBlocks.title: Explain and retry
contentBlocks.description: Provide reasoning-focused feedback and allow revision without creating scored assessment eligibility.

contentBlocks.title: Technical information and source boundary
contentBlocks.description: Reinforce that vehicle-specific procedures, specifications, limits, and safety instructions require applicable authoritative information.

contentBlocks.title: Foundations summary
contentBlocks.description: Summarize how systems thinking, safety, professional practice, evidence, and documentation support later automotive coursework.

visuals.title: Major vehicle-system relationships
visuals.purpose: Show high-level relationships among vehicle systems without presenting a vehicle-specific schematic.

visuals.title: Concern-to-next-step workflow
visuals.purpose: Show the sequence from concern through evidence gathering and documentation.

visuals.title: Evidence versus conclusion
visuals.purpose: Compare concerns, observations, measurements, references, hypotheses, and conclusions.

visuals.title: Automotive learning foundations
visuals.purpose: Summarize systems thinking, safety, professional practice, evidence, technical information, and documentation.

practiceTasks: Match common vehicle functions to the major system most directly responsible for them
Sort sample statements into concern, observation, measurement, reference, hypothesis, or conclusion
Identify which information must be verified before following a vehicle-specific procedure
Write a brief rationale for a safe next step in a basic guided concern
lessonContentPlans.evidenceExpectation: Technical claims require approved provenance. Vehicle-specific procedures, values, limits, and specifications require an appropriate authoritative source and must not be invented.
lessonContentPlans.assessmentBoundary: Training checks may coach, explain, and allow retry. Scored assessment remains a separate approval state and requires provenance, review status, curriculum mapping, and secure delivery.

lessonContentPlans.lessonSummary: Develop a disciplined approach to automotive shop safety, hazardous-material and environmental awareness, tool and equipment boundaries, high-voltage hazard recognition, documentation, and professional responsibility without substituting generic instruction for applicable site, product, vehicle, or regulatory requirements.
prerequisites: No formal course prerequisite
AUT 101 foundations recommended for curriculum sequence

learningObjectives.statement: Identify common categories of automotive shop hazards and distinguish hazard recognition from authorization to perform a specific task.
Use applicable safety, environmental, equipment, product, and technical information to determine whether work may proceed, requires additional controls, or should stop and be escalated.
Document observed hazards, selected controls, professional communication, and the reason for a safe next action without inventing limits, procedures, or regulatory requirements.

contentBlocks.title: Lesson targets
contentBlocks.description: Preview the hazard-recognition, information-use, documentation, and professional-decision outcomes for the lesson.

contentBlocks.title: Safety starts before the task
contentBlocks.description: Connect prior shop experience to the principle that recognizing a task is not the same as being authorized, equipped, or informed to perform it.

contentBlocks.title: Hazard categories in automotive work
contentBlocks.description: Organize hazards around work areas, materials, tools and equipment, electrical or stored energy, and environmental conditions without assigning universal thresholds.

contentBlocks.title: Recognize, verify, control, document, escalate
contentBlocks.description: Use a conceptual process model for moving from a recognized hazard to an information-supported professional action.

contentBlocks.title: When the safest next step is to stop
contentBlocks.description: Demonstrate how an unclear hazard, missing information, or uncertain authorization can lead to a documented stop-work and escalation decision rather than an improvised procedure.

contentBlocks.title: Hazard and information sorting
contentBlocks.description: Classify sample observations by hazard category and identify what applicable information would be needed before proceeding.

contentBlocks.title: Safe next-action scenario
contentBlocks.description: Select whether to proceed, add controls, stop, or escalate in a generalized shop scenario and justify the decision using the information available.

contentBlocks.title: Safety reasoning check
contentBlocks.description: Use low-stakes formative prompts to check hazard recognition, information selection, documentation, and escalation reasoning.

contentBlocks.title: Explain the safer choice and retry
contentBlocks.description: Provide reasoning-focused feedback and allow revision without creating scored assessment eligibility.

contentBlocks.title: Applicable information governs the task
contentBlocks.description: Reinforce that site rules, product information, equipment instructions, vehicle-specific information, and applicable legal or regulatory requirements must be verified rather than invented.

contentBlocks.title: Professional safety practice summary
contentBlocks.description: Summarize hazard recognition, information use, controls, documentation, stop-work authority, escalation, and professional communication as foundations for later technical work.

visuals.title: Automotive shop hazard categories
visuals.purpose: Show broad hazard categories and their relationships without presenting universal limits or task-specific procedures.

visuals.title: Proceed, control, stop, or escalate
visuals.purpose: Show an information-supported decision path from observed condition to professional next action.

visuals.title: Hazard versus required information
visuals.purpose: Compare hazard categories with the kinds of applicable information that may be needed before work proceeds.

visuals.title: Safe and professional work habits
visuals.purpose: Summarize recognition, verification, control, documentation, communication, and escalation.

practiceTasks: Classify generalized shop observations by hazard category
Identify what applicable information should be checked before a task proceeds
Choose between proceed, add controls, stop, or escalate for a generalized scenario
Write a brief professional hazard and next-action note
assessmentPlan: Formative stop-work or escalation reasoning scenario

lessonContentPlans.lessonSummary: Develop disciplined use of service information, wiring diagrams, technical specifications, diagnostic procedures, and digital technical resources with emphasis on applicability, provenance, interpretation, and documentation.
prerequisites: AUT 101
Orientation to the AutoLearnPro learning environment

learningObjectives.statement: Explain the core concepts and relationships represented in Automotive Technical Documentation and Service Information without treating a general instructional model as a vehicle-specific procedure.
Distinguish observations, measurements, source information, assumptions, and conclusions when working with automotive technical documentation and service information evidence.
Use applicable technical information and documented evidence to justify a safe next learning or diagnostic step while identifying information that still requires authoritative verification.

contentBlocks.title: Lesson targets
contentBlocks.description: Preview the conceptual, evidence, and source-use outcomes for Automotive Technical Documentation and Service Information.

contentBlocks.title: Connect prior knowledge
contentBlocks.description: Activate relevant prior learning while separating general familiarity from verified technical information.

contentBlocks.title: Core system and concept relationships
contentBlocks.description: Explain the major relationships identified by the catalog description for Automotive Technical Documentation and Service Information.

contentBlocks.title: Concept relationship model
contentBlocks.description: Use a simplified instructional model to organize relationships without implying a universal vehicle architecture, specification, or procedure.

contentBlocks.title: Evidence to next step
contentBlocks.description: Demonstrate how a generalized concern or task moves from information gathering to a justified next step without inventing technical values or procedures.

contentBlocks.title: Evidence and source sorting
contentBlocks.description: Classify sample information as observation, measurement, source statement, assumption, or conclusion and identify missing applicability information.

contentBlocks.title: Generalized application scenario
contentBlocks.description: Choose and justify an information-supported next step in a generalized scenario while preserving source and safety boundaries.

contentBlocks.title: Formative reasoning check
contentBlocks.description: Use low-stakes prompts to check conceptual understanding, evidence classification, source selection, and next-step reasoning.

contentBlocks.title: Explain and retry
contentBlocks.description: Provide reasoning-focused feedback and allow revision without creating scored assessment eligibility.

contentBlocks.title: Applicable information and provenance
contentBlocks.description: Reinforce that vehicle-, product-, equipment-, legal-, regulatory-, and specification-dependent claims require applicable authoritative information.

contentBlocks.title: Lesson summary
contentBlocks.description: Summarize the concepts, evidence habits, source boundaries, and documentation practices for Automotive Technical Documentation and Service Information.

visuals.title: Automotive Technical Documentation and Service Information concept relationships
visuals.purpose: Show the major instructional relationships without presenting a vehicle-specific diagram or specification.

visuals.title: Evidence-to-next-step workflow
visuals.purpose: Show a generalized sequence from task or concern through evidence, applicable information, and documented next action.

visuals.title: Observation, source, assumption, and conclusion
visuals.purpose: Compare evidence categories and the information required before a technical conclusion is supported.

visuals.title: Automotive Technical Documentation and Service Information learning framework
visuals.purpose: Summarize concepts, evidence, source verification, reasoning, and documentation.

practiceTasks: Identify the major concepts or system relationships in a generalized Automotive Technical Documentation and Service Information example
Sort sample information into observation, measurement, source statement, assumption, or conclusion
Identify what authoritative information would be required before applying a specification or procedure
Write a brief evidence-based rationale for a safe next step
lessonContentPlans.evidenceExpectation: Technical claims require approved provenance. Vehicle-specific procedures, specifications, numeric limits, product or equipment instructions, legal or regulatory requirements, and authorization rules require applicable authoritative information and must not be invented.
